lines.text: A five-year-old boy needs a bronchoscopy for a suspected inhaled peanut. Where is it most likely to be?
Start at the right main bronchus.
It is wider, shorter and runs more vertically than the left main bronchus.
So inhaled foreign bodies more commonly enter the right lung.
The left main bronchus is narrower and less vertical: the less likely path.
Because of gravity, the right lower lobe is most likely to receive the peanut.
So the answer is the right lower lobe bronchus.
